labels.note: Plain ask for time; sending the link is reversible and deterministic.
Negation scopes to the move, so no move intent; the grumbling is dismissed third-party noise, not a complaint.
A broken code is a defect Max cannot diagnose; it is not a commercial money conversation.
Unambiguous ask for time.
Retraction of an earlier move request; nothing live remains to act on.
Live defect report; hand over, do not diagnose.
Ask for time; send the link.
Instruction to hold off on a possible cancellation; negation means no cancel intent yet.
A failed test is a live blocker Max must not interpret.
Ask for time today; send the link.
Explicit do-not-reschedule; negation leaves no move intent.
Is-this-normal about slow behaviour is the not-sure-if-a-bug shape; answering would assert an unverifiable fact.
Terse ask for time on a named day.
States explicitly that nothing changed; no commitment or scheduling intent.
Stale balance is a live data defect; hand over.
Terse but the only reading is a request for time.
Hypothetical plus an explicit statement that it is not a request; no intent.
Live hardware/output failure affecting operations; Max cannot diagnose.
A client-placed hold is a scheduling ask; confirming or declining is reversible and deterministic.
Hypothetical framing kills any booking action, but the live question is about capacity and scope, which Max may never state.
Asks for Max's judgment on whether a metric shift matters; opinions on their business are lane C.
Ask for availability; send the link.
Hypothetical outage carries no problem intent, but who-answers-during-an-incident is a coverage guarantee Max must not make.
Past/resolved rule: the issue is closed and was on their side, so no live problem; the apology warrants a reaction, not a reply.
Direct availability request.
The do-not-build clause blocks work but the feasibility/scope question is still live and only a person may answer it.
Device-specific failure is a live defect; the does-that-make-sense ask is exactly the diagnosis Max must not attempt.
Booking with someone on the client's team is still our meeting, not the third-party case.
Third-party meeting plus a lateness FYI; no request to shift our call.
Explicitly still happening, so not covered by the resolved rule.
Request for an hour this week; send the link.
Third-party vendor's call, explicitly disclaimed as not ours.
Resolved and retracted with a stated cause on their side; no live problem, apology gets a reaction.
Request for a recurring slot is a scheduling ask; setting or linking a cadence is reversible.
Third-party meeting they will escalate only if it becomes ours.
A reported figure changing for the same day is a live data defect, not a billing question.
Direct ask for time this afternoon.
Relayed acknowledgement of a message with a reply promised; nothing to act on, react at most.
Scoped down but still live and explicitly asks for someone to look; a card is mentioned, no card number, so no PII.
Explicit request for an invite.
Client-internal staffing update, explicitly disclaimed as nothing for the agency.
Partial failure with a hung state is a live defect.
Offer of in-person time is a scheduling ask; the link is the reversible response.
Idiom plus a decision settled months ago; past/resolved, no live intent.
Should-this-be-visible is a live possible-bug report; confirming intended behaviour would assert a fact Max cannot verify.
Shift of an existing call; send the link.
Mentions a past meeting but carries no scheduling intent; the live ask is for notes, a doc they already have access to.
Live data defect plus stated loss of trust and withdrawal, a churn-adjacent dissatisfaction signal.
Blanket reschedule, not a cancellation; overwhelm here is context, not a complaint about the work.
Instruction not to read a stale doc; the negation leaves no resource request.
Correction narrows the defect but keeps it live.
Ask to shift an existing call later.
Internal status FYI that explicitly requires nothing from us.
Orders missing required data with work blocked is a live defect.
Existing session must shift because an attendee is out; send the link.
A delivery blocker a person should see; the legal reference is routine internal review, not lawyers/dispute/liability, so lane D does not fire.
Duplicate charge from one payment action is a live defect; order references are not PII, and no money terms are being asked of Max.
Reordering two existing sessions is a reschedule.
Explicitly asks humans on our side to weigh in on an idea; opinion on the work is lane C.
Contradictory values for the same record is a live defect; low urgency does not change the lane.
Recurring call clashes; ask to shift it.
Idiom rule: a system being down is an outage, and nothing here asks for time despite the word bookings.
Scratch-that only corrects the detail; the defect is explicitly still live.
Idiomatic ask to shift an existing slot later.
Sense is explicitly disambiguated to mean discuss, not defer, so there is no cancel intent; the live ask is to talk, and a link is reversible.
Not covered by the resolved rule: the client escalates the silent self-correction itself as the live integrity concern.
Reschedule; the warehouse aside is their internal context, not a problem report to us.
Negation clears one area only; the other is a live problem in its own clause.
Textbook not-sure-if-a-bug report with reproducible behaviour; live problem.
Ask to shift an existing slot; send the link.
A repeatedly unanswered ask is dissatisfaction on top of a live defect; the refund here is a broken feature, not a billing request.
Will-it-be-ready-by-the-date question Max may never answer, plus a live test failure.
Reschedule to next week, not a cancellation.
Read as intent, not words: the sarcasm about the wait is a dissatisfaction signal a person must handle.
A small defect is still a defect; size does not change the lane.
Cancellation: act, offer rebooking, and post internally because it is a health signal.
Sarcasm about scope growth is dissatisfaction with the work, not a scope question being asked.
Live data-loss defect; an email address is not on the policy's PII list (ID, card, bank, password), so lane D does not fire.
Cannot attend an existing call: cancel, offer the rebooking link, notify.
The not-a-criticism hedge is a disclaimer, not a negation; the substance is dissatisfaction with delivery practice.
Is-this-supposed-to question about duplicated input is a live possible-bug report.
Calls off this week's session; cancel and notify.
Joke, self-retracted in the same message; urgency wording is not an intent.
Regression: previously closed, now reproducing again, so the resolved rule does not apply.
Cancelling a standing series is a cancellation; act, offer rebooking, notify.
Cross-customer data exposure is a live defect; the message contains no ID, card, bank or password, so lane D does not fire.
Working-as-built but causing tickets is still a live problem; Max must not adjudicate intended behaviour.
Drops an existing slot; cancel, offer rebooking, notify.
Minimising framing does not change a live reporting defect with stated business impact.
Two live defects reported together; Max cannot diagnose either.
Take it off the calendar is a cancellation; act and notify.
Failed charges on the account are billing, which is lane C; last four digits are not a card number, so lane D does not fire.
Degradation report with a buried question; the not-a-complaint disclaimer does not make it not a problem.
Explicit cancellation; act, offer rebooking, notify.
Explicitly instructs no action until a proper message follows; no live intent.
Still-want-it-closed keeps it live despite the one-off framing.
Calls off the session outright; cancel, offer rebooking, notify.
Explicitly states someone on their side owns it and we need not pick it up.
Vague but live quality problem plus dissatisfaction with the delivered work; the rework-scope ask also needs a person.
Explicit cancellation of a specific session; act and notify.
No cancel intent (negation); confirming the session still stands is verifiable and non-committal, and silence has a cost while a rumour spreads.
